- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75.0), model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply a downward correction of 3–8% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) for 3+ consecutive days, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–4% to account for bearish sentiment reversal.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon (days 1–5) when sentiment is neutral or positive; cap forecast for first 3 days at 1–2% below historical mean of recent 10-day window.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 10-day moving average of true values if sentiment shifts mid-horizon.
- If sentiment is high but price action shows no breakout (e.g., no >75.0 spike), reduce forecast volatility; cap 30d forecast range within ±3% of 14-day moving average.
